description: Preparing for La Niña is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Pacific Regional Integrated Sciences and Assessments (Pacific RISA); Pacific Islands Regional Climate Assessment. O'ahu's busy construction industry depends on being able to dispose of demolition and construction wastes. Forecasts for a developing La Niña (often accompanied by heavy rains in Hawai'i) alerted managers at the island's main construction landfill to their climate vulnerability. Coverage: the United States (2016). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
